newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI confirms may list coal after Shell deal.
newsitem.headline: JCI confirms may list coal after Shell deal.

text.p: JCI Ltd confirmed on Tuesday it was considering a separate listing of its coal assets following its decision to purchase Shell South Africa's coal interests.

Shell International Ltd said on Tuesday that it had signed a letter of intent to sell its 50 percent share in the Rietspruit joint venture with Ingwe Coal Corp, a 6.82 percent share in the Richards Bay Coal Terminal Company (RBCT) and some 2.1 billion tonnes of coal reserves.

"The acquisition of Shell South Africa's coal assets and in particular the RBCT entitlement will increase export potential which in turn, with the larger synergistic resource base, could lead to the development of new mines," said JCI managing director Bill Nairn in a statement.
"It also represents an opportunity to enhance the rating of JCI Limited's coal assets and this rating may be further enhanced through a possible listing of these assets in due course."
Analysts had told Reuters earlier they expected JCI to list its coal assets separately in the wake of the Shell deal.
They said that the bulk of the purchase price, rumoured to be between 400 and 500 million rand, appeared to be for the RBCT stake.
